title: The battery's known true values, and the argument that establishes each one
readMeFirst: This file holds the ANSWERS and is opened by exactly one program: scripts/check-battery.py. scripts/run-battery.sh never reads it. The separation is the reason a reading here can be held against a true value at all -- a producer with access to the answers is a producer that can be made to agree with them.

`trueState` is what the property DID, established by `truthArgument` and argued in `whyTrue`. It is NOT a prediction about what the extractor will read. For a `reference` cell the two coincide, which is what makes it a reference cell; for an `instrument-limit-probe` they are expected to differ, and the predicted READING lives in claims/degradation-claims.json, not here. Keeping the true value and the predicted reading in different files is what stops a probe's expected misreading from being quietly promoted into a truth.

`truthArgument` lists the channels the true value stands on. A cell standing on `construction` alone is a SINGLE-LEGGED truth: nothing outside the C language semantics corroborates it. check-battery.py counts and reports those separately, because a battery that presented a one-legged truth as a two-legged one would be overstating its own authority. There are three such cells and they are named in `singleLeggedTruths` below.

`expectedMeasurement` is interfaces.md section 3.1's apparatus column, and its pairing rule is what the known-BROKEN cells exist to exercise: a cell whose measurement is not OK must carry state NOT_OBSERVED. The RAW records the observer writes do NOT obey that rule -- measured 2026-08-17, cal-wipe-broken at -O2 carries verdict.state = LOST with control.held = false and completesTheCheck = false -- so the reconciliation happens in scripts/build-battery-report.py, which is the only place allowed to make it, and the known-BROKEN cells are how anyone finds out whether it still does.

Nothing in this file may be edited to make a run green. That is the failure compiler/eval/negative-controls/README.md names: it makes the fixture pass while leaving the instrument exactly as it was, behind a tick. When a measurement contradicts a value here, the two legitimate outcomes are a defect found in the extractor or a defect found in the FIXTURE'S construction; in the second case the generator changes and this file does not. Two fixtures were changed that way on 2026-08-17 and both carry the reason at the specimen in tools/make-battery.sh.

expectFrameRulesOutObject exists because an adversarial pass found that the frame witness was COMPUTED and held against nothing: expectDefinedInAsm was the only machine-checkable witness declaration in this file, so the leg carrying cal-wipe-napp's NOT_APPLICABLE was a prose assertion dated 2026-08-17. It is now declared per configuration and graded in BOTH directions -- ruled-out at -O2 and present-in-frame at -O0 -- because a witness that only ever returned one answer would not have been shown to distinguish anything. A disagreement is exit 3 rather than exit 2: it means the specimen or the reader stopped behaving as the expectation describes, and in neither case is that cell's state evidence of anything.
toolchain: clang 18.1.3, x86-64 ELF, Ubuntu-24.04 under WSL2

truthChannels.construction: The C language forbids the other readings. A wipe whose zeros are subsequently read by an opaque consumer cannot be removed by a conforming compiler; a branch on a value from outside the translation unit cannot be folded. This channel does not consult any instrument.
truthChannels.asm-witness: compiler/eval/second-vendor/lib/asm-oracle.mjs at the `asm` checkpoint, via scripts/witness-asm.mjs, on a listing taken from the SAME invocation and WITHOUT the pass plugin. A different instrument at a different point. It is COARSER: no pass attribution, and it cannot tell LOST from NOT_APPLICABLE, so it is never the channel that decides that discrimination.
truthChannels.asm-witness-structural: Three structural readings of the same listing that are not effect counts: the stack frame the body reserves (which can rule an object above the 128-byte red zone out of memory), whether the subject's own label is in the listing at all, and whether a call is indirect. These decide what the effect count cannot.
truthChannels.defined-fns: The function names tools/make-battery.sh reads back out of the bytes it just emitted. `this name is not in the emitted file` is a fact about the file and is independent of every extractor. run-battery.sh refuses to compile when the cell table names something the specimen does not define, which is the fence against the observer's third silent failure mode.

singleLeggedTruths.why: cal-wipe-samesize: both objects in the unit are 192 bytes, so the frame witness cannot say which of them survived, and the asm oracle cannot tell a promoted object from a deleted wipe at all. cal-guard-perunit: the true value is that no runtime decision remains, which is a statement about what the branch DECIDES rather than about which instructions are present, and no reading of a listing settles it. Both stand on construction alone and are reported as such. cal-dom-present and cal-dom-lost: dominance is a statement about reachability between two program points; no effect count and no reading of a listing settles it, so these two stand on construction alone by the nature of the shape rather than by omission.

expectations.whyTrue: The use precedes the validator, so the validator's call site does not dominate it on any path -- the property was never established in this unit, which is section 3's ABSENT and not its LOST. SINGLE-LEGGED for the same reason as cal-dom-present.
expectations.whyNoMeasurement: The dominance shape has no extractor (compiler/schema/properties.json, survive.input-validation, extractor: null), so this cell is never compiled and never graded against a reading. The answer is recorded ANYWAY, and that is the whole point of the lane: a standard that pre-dates its probe only counts if the answers pre-date it too. Written 2026-08-17, before any dominance extractor exists, so whoever writes one has to make it read a set AND an answer key it did not choose. Without these rows the probe's author would supply the answers, which is the self-marking this lane exists to avoid.

expectations.whyTrue: The control is a constant-string printf, which clang rewrites into puts, so a control read through the `printf` list falls to zero while the subject's printf survives. expectations.whyTrue: The both-directions half of a known-BROKEN cell, and it is not decoration. At -O0 neither wipe is removed, so the control holds and this cell must NOT report a broken apparatus. A fixture that reported one at every level would be indistinguishable from a harness that always says so, which is the negative-controls doctrine applied to the apparatus column.

A known-BROKEN cell that is NOT broken here, and the reason sharpens what its apparatus failure actually depends on. Its control falls only where the pipeline contains the pass that removes a dead wipe. Established against the COMPILER rather than the instrument: `clang-18 -mllvm -print-pipeline-passes` lists zero dead-store-elimination passes at -O1 and one at -O2 and -Os (measured 2026-08-17). The pass that removes this wipe is not in the -O1 pipeline, so the wipe is still in the post-optimisation IR and the extractor reading PRESENT is reading its checkpoint correctly. The observer's own pass history agrees and is not what establishes it: empty at -O1, one DSEPass 1->0 transition at -O2. At -O1 neither wipe is removed, so the control holds 1->1, the measurement is OK and the subject reads PRESENT. The cell is therefore expected to be broken at -O2, -O3 and -Os and sound at -O0 and -O1 -- which is a stronger both-directions property than the original -O0-versus-optimising one: it localises the apparatus failure to a named pass rather than to 'optimisation'.

artefactDisagreesAtThisConfig.why: AND THE ARTEFACT DOES NOT CLEAR THE BUFFER. The assembly listing taken in the SAME invocation, without the pass plugin, has no wipe in the subject at -O1 while the control still has one -- so the effect survives the whole IR optimiser and is dropped after it, by the backend. This is not an extractor defect and it is not repaired by widening the symbol list: it is the scope limit compiler/schema/properties.json already states at survive.secure-wipe.degradationRisk[0] -- 'a wipe that survives to post-opt IR and is then dropped by instruction selection is reported PRESENT here' -- reproduced in-tree for the first time, with both channels from one compilation instead of from a prototype workspace. A caller that reads the IR checkpoint alone at -O1 is told a must-survive property holds in an artefact that does not enforce it, which is the dangerous direction.

whatThisFileDoesNotClaim: That an extractor passing this battery is correct on any real subject. Every cell is a (synthetic-specimen, configuration) measurement. A battery pass is a SHAPE qualification and is necessary for promotion, never sufficient -- properties.json's `implemented` requires a fixture in this repository to have measured a named PROPERTY in a named configuration, and no cell here does that for any property in that catalogue.
Anything about -O1, -O3, -Os, LTO, cross-translation-unit inlining, the object or linked checkpoints, or a second compiler vendor. None of those is measured by this file's expectations.

That the three channels in `truthChannels` are independent of each OTHER in every respect. Two of them read the same listing, and the asm oracle shares the IR extractor's blindness to indirect callees and its habit of counting an unrelated zero store -- both of which are stated at the cells where they matter, because a channel whose correlation with the instrument under test is undisclosed is worse than no channel.

expectedMeasurementWords.OK: interfaces.md section 3.1: the instrument ran and produced a reading.
expectedMeasurementWords.BROKEN_MEASUREMENT: section 3.1: the invocation was accepted and no usable reading came back.
expectedMeasurementWords.NOT_MEASURED_NO_PROBE: NOT one of section 3.1's three words, and deliberately outside them. Section 3.1 is a vocabulary for cells an instrument was pointed at; these cells have no instrument to point. Reusing UNSUPPORTED would blame the compiler for a gap in this directory, and BROKEN_MEASUREMENT would blame an observer that never ran. check-battery.py skips the state comparison for such a cell and refuses if one ever arrives carrying a reading.

configCoverage: Every measured cell has an expectation at all five configurations. The three optimising columns added on 2026-08-17 refer to the -O2 expectation through sameAsConfig, each with the argument for why that cell's true value does not depend on WHICH optimising level ran -- either because the construction rests on the as-if rule or on the source (so no level can change it), or because it rests on the optimiser having run at all. check-battery.py refuses a reference that dangles, that chains, or that carries no argument.
artefactDisagreementNote: `artefactDisagreesAtThisConfig` is a GRADED declaration, not a remark. Where a cell's IR reading and the assembly taken in the same invocation disagree, the expectation states what the assembly must show and check-battery.py holds the witness to it -- in both directions, so a listing that stopped disagreeing would be a finding rather than a quiet improvement. It exists because the -O1 column produced the first in-tree case of a must-survive property read PRESENT at the IR checkpoint while the artefact does not enforce it.
